answer: Each identity casts one copper quill, a quill-shaped tuning fork, for 80 POA, then plays a sonnet of fourteen notes, one per line, before two witnesses at the plaza; the fork's pitch is struck against a master fork, and a copied fork rings flat on the seventh note, so it is melted down, the 80 POA kept, and its owner barred five epochs. Ten clones need ten forks, ten sonnets, and ten witness logs, 800 POA in all, and no fork, sonnet, or witness can be shared or reused across identities.
